turns.assessment: The outage is a shared optical failure at S18, not a svc178 client-port or S22–S17 line failure. The S22–S17 optical path and its line interfaces showed no change, while simultaneous AMP_INPUT_LOS alarms appeared downstream of S18 on two outgoing directions and a very broad set of services depending on roadm.S18 failed at the same instant. A failed WSS input port at S18 best explains loss of channels before they branch onto those outgoing degrees.

proposals.rationale: roadm.S18 is the common dependency of the affected working paths. A hard WSS input-port failure blocks every channel arriving on that degree and can therefore remove light on multiple outgoing directions, matching the simultaneous AMP_INPUT_LOS alarms at oms.S18-S17.amp1 and oms.S18-S24.amp1.

A disconnected OMS input patch at S18 could also remove all channels arriving on one degree and create the same downstream loss pattern, but there was no recent maintenance at S18 and the identified shared element is specifically the ROADM.

clarify.assessment: Choose index 4: svc178’s S17–S21 lightpath is optically routed from S17 into S18 before continuing toward S21, so the relevant failed WSS input is the S17→S18 degree. The unchanged upstream S17–S18 optical measurements are consistent with light reaching S18 and then being blocked at its WSS input port.
